key_insight: Topology-guided regional latent dynamics enable accurate full-field prediction of transient nonlinear structural responses on large finite element meshes.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate targets time-history prediction for heterogeneous structures, including stiffened panels and million-node vehicle crash models.
method: Encode mesh responses into regional latent states using engineering priors and topology-constrained interactions.
Improve latent dynamics with auxiliary one-step prediction and forecast trajectories using load-conditioned spatiotemporal Mamba.
Reconstruct full-field nodal responses with a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three FEM datasets, TPLD reports 1.41%–12.22% displacement-component relative L2 errors on an approximately 1.49-million-node vehicle and 0.620% position error on the BIW benchmark, 30.7% below the best GeoTransolver configuration.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen structural topologies and loading regimes is not established by the abstract; regional partitioning also requires mesh and engineering priors.
paper_title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction
